claims.text: Sequence's file picker is a trained ranker that reads file contents, history and paths. On 8 held-out repositories it put a file the real fix changed in its top five 84.9% of the time, against 51.0% for grep (internal test; the repositories are not in this tree).

It learns from what the agent changes. In each repository the file finder checks which files the agent actually edited, and retrains on that. It switches to the new version only if it tests no worse than the old one. All of it stays on your computer.

It learns from failures too. When a request keeps going wrong (asked twice, stopped, rewritten, or reported not done), Sequence proposes a short note for the repository, quoting those turns. You accept or dismiss it. Accepted notes go into later prompts; a note after which those failures come back more often is flagged for you and left out of later prompts.
Refine notes: after work that fell short, the app can propose a short note for your project. Nothing is added until you Accept. Adding notes without asking is off by default.
Accept adds one line to `.sequence/memory/NOTES.md`. Undo removes that line. Nothing is written without an Accept.
Add notes without asking — Applies to every project. Even on, a note in the agent's words still waits for you.
claims.gap: OFF (as labelled; no plan needed)

"At any repository size" for "a question" in general overreaches. The agent arm of agent-context-bench (per-question input tokens as the agent reports them, 4 repo sizes, plan 2.7) is BUILT and its plumbing proven with a mock agent; the live numbers are not yet measured or published
